groups.title: Plan and set up
groups.summary: Before the first line of code: turn the plan into a timeline, and make sure anyone can run the repo from a fresh clone.

groups.title: Review
groups.summary: A second opinion on the code and the interface, ranked by what is most likely to hurt you in production or cost you a conversion.

groups.title: Maintain and ship
groups.summary: The chores that pile up: patching dependencies, clearing the PR queue, and checking the deploy actually went out.

groups.title: Grow
groups.summary: After it ships: write about it, get it found in search and AI answers, and run a weekly loop on the numbers.

items.name: gantarr
items.summary: Turns a plan, roadmap, or the conversation so far into a valid Gantarr JSON file you can import to render a Gantt chart.

items.name: groundwork
items.summary: Walks the fresh-clone path for real, scores local dev readiness, fixes the gaps, and opens one PR with a before/after scorecard.

items.name: sentinel
items.summary: Audits the whole repo for quality, test coverage, CI, security, and AI-agent fragility, ranked by production risk.

items.name: design-review
items.summary: Reviews a UI for conversion, UX, accessibility, and performance against Apple, FT, and OpenAI standards, and calls out AI design slop.

items.name: warden
items.summary: Pulls production errors, then patches security alerts and bumps dependencies, verified by your own build and tests, in one PR.

items.name: conductor
items.summary: Merges every ready PR newest first, each one green on CI, then confirms the deploy shipped and the live app answers.

items.name: blogger
items.summary: Turns shipped commits into dated blog posts, changelog entries, and social snippets written in your site's voice.

items.name: beacon
items.summary: Reviews SEO and AI-answer visibility from Search Console, Ahrefs, and PostHog data, then fixes pages, metadata, and schema.

items.name: growth-review
items.summary: Runs a weekly growth loop: health checks, this week against last, a dated log entry, then ships the one highest-leverage change.

changes.text: Every skill can now be installed on its own with the skills CLI, into any agent it supports.
Walks the fresh-clone path, scores ten setup steps, fixes the gaps, and opens one PR with the before/after scorecard.
Also checks test coverage (is there a command, does CI enforce it, which critical paths are untested) and whether deploys are automated and gated on CI.

Added /warden security: collects every open high and critical Dependabot, code scanning, and secret scanning alert across a repo, a list of repos, or an org, and opens one PR that fixes or triages them.
Merges security-sweep PRs first, then re-counts open high and critical alerts after the deploy.
Releases are now versioned with changesets, so /plugin marketplace update pulls new skills reliably.
The weekly loop: check the site is actually up and tracking, log the week's numbers, then build one improvement.
The plugin and marketplace are now both called joshghent-skills.
SEO and GEO review driven by real Search Console, Ahrefs, and PostHog data, including whether AI crawlers are allowed in.
A merge train for ready PRs that never force-merges, then watches the deploy and smoke-checks the live app.
Prioritises the dependency sweep by live production errors from Sentry, New Relic, Cloudflare Workers, and others.
Fixed the plugin install so Claude Code discovers every skill.
Plan in, importable Gantt timeline out, validated before it is handed over.
All skills bundled into a single plugin, so install is two commands at most.
A senior product designer's critique of a rendered UI, across viewports and keyboard states.
Dependency and security maintenance, including end-of-life runtime upgrades to the current LTS.
The repo became a Claude Code plugin marketplace.
The first two skills: turn commits into blog posts, and audit a repo for risk.
